analysis: Both changed files are Swift test files under libs/darkbloom-cluster/Tests; no production code is touched in the supplied units. Gemma4TensorParallelTests.swift (added, lines 444-609 visible) uses synthetic weights and CPU-only threads. It covers shard-vs-whole operation diagnostics (gated by the GEMMA_TP_DIAG env var), an FP32 oracle token comparison, and vocabulary-split greedy, top-k and row-gather tests. It performs no network, key, attestation or cache I/O. The only filesystem use is a temporary synthetic model directory that the test removes in a defer. ResidentAdmissionGemma4Tests.swift changes line 495 only, so the expectation now includes .tensorParallel in supportedGenerationModes for the three Gemma rows. That asserts a production capability-metadata change made elsewhere in the PR (not supplied in this batch). Relevant threat model items are TB-002 and TB-007, plus A-001 for the plaintext residual and logits crossing between ranks. The unseen production tensor-parallel implementation matters: whether the rank-to-rank reduction and logits gather (JACCL) stay on the existing admission and arithmetic-environment gating, and whether advertising tensorParallel affects coordinator routing or any attestation/capability surface. The integration pass should verify those. Only test code was reviewed here, and the first 443 lines of the added test file and its production counterparts were not available, so coverage is partial. No concrete security regression is evident in the visible lines.
